sections.h2: Who records deeds in Clearfield County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Register and Recorder's Office on the first floor of the Clearfield County Courthouse records them. The office phone is 814-765-2641, extension 5012. The county provides six public workstations there for finding documents filed in the office.

The Recorder of Deeds division takes all documents relating to real estate, plus notary public bonds and commissions, UCC filings and military discharges. It also issues copies and certified copies.

For a house seller in Clearfield County, the recorder is the final step. After the deed is signed at closing, it goes to this office, and the recording is what makes the new owner's title part of the public record.

sections.h2: Why does a Clearfield County deed need a UPI stamp first?
sections.html:
Every deed has to be presented to the county's Uniform Parcel Identifier office for a UPI stamp before the recorder will take it. The fee is $10 per parcel, and the questions line is 814-765-2641, extension 2042. The recorder's own page says deeds can be pre-approved for the UPI before the day of recording.

That step catches sellers who treat recording as a single stop. A title agent normally sends the deed to the UPI office a day or two ahead, receives the stamp, and then submits the stamped deed with the fee and tax checks. A seller closing without a title company should ask the county how the pre-approval works.

The recorder's page repeats the rule in its list of deed requirements: every deed must carry the UPI stamp from the Assessment Office.

sections.h2: How much will the Clearfield County recorder bill me?
sections.html:
A deed or a mortgage is $79.75 on the fee schedule posted on the county's Recorder of Deeds page, a schedule marked effective March 27, 2020. Names over four cost 50 cents each, and each page over four adds $2. The posted schedule also says that where no fee is specified, the Recorder of Deeds sets one.

sections.h2: When does a Clearfield County deed need a Statement of Value?
sections.html:
The recorder's page says a Statement of Value is required when the full consideration is not written in the deed, when the deed is a gift or carries no value, when a tax exemption is claimed, or when the property was sold at a tax claim sale or a sheriff's sale. It is also required when the real estate passes by will through an estate. The form must be filed, signed and dated.

The page lists one case where the form is not required: a transfer that is exempt because of a family relationship, defined as grandparent, parent, child, brother or sister.

The tax itself is described on the state's revenue pages. It is 1 percent at the state level, county recorders collect it, often with a local tax, and buyer and seller are both liable. Exempt categories include certain family transfers, property passing by will or intestacy, and farms.

  • A signed certificate of address for the buyer must be on the deed.
  • The deed must give the municipality and county of the property.
  • When land crosses municipal or school district lines, the document must give the percentage in each so the local tax is divided correctly.
  • The acknowledgment date cannot come before the date of the document.

sections.h2: What can a Clearfield County owner search before listing?
sections.html:
Two search products are open to the public. Landex Remote is the full tool, with the same search criteria as the software in the courthouse, and it suits someone who searches often. Landex Webstore is the basic version for occasional use; it can search several counties at once and narrow results by county, instrument type and municipality. Images can be viewed only after a credit card payment. For help with the online products, the county lists an information line at 717-274-5890.

A seller can use either to pull the last recorded deed, any open mortgage, and any easement or right of way that will show up in a title search.

sections.h2: What other rules does the Clearfield County office enforce?
sections.html:
The office rejects documents with a defective acknowledgment, meaning one missing the county, state, date, the name of the person or corporate officer appearing, the notary's signature, seal or expiration date. It also says no blanket assignments, releases or satisfactions will be accepted.

  • Re-recorded or corrective documents must state the reason and carry a new acknowledgment.
  • Several documents from one transaction must be numbered in the order they should be recorded.
  • Foreign language documents need a written English translation.
  • Every package needs a return envelope, stamped and addressed, big enough for the document.

Electronic recording is available through Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and CSC at 866-652-0111. A seller whose title company already uses one of them can skip the courier. The county also runs a free Landex Record Alert program that sends an email or text if someone tries to record a deed under an owner's name or parcel number. Signing up takes the parcel number printed under Map # on the tax invoice.

sections.h2: What does Clearfield County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Clearfield County is the third largest Pennsylvania county by land area, with 1,145 square miles, and it sits in the north central part of the state. The West Branch Susquehanna River cuts through the borough of Clearfield, the county seat. DuBois is the largest city, with 7,794 people in the 2010 census, followed by Clearfield borough at 6,215 and Curwensville at 2,542.

The county was created in 1804 from parts of Huntingdon and Lycoming counties and organized in 1822. Lumber and coal were its two big industries from the mid-1800s into the early 1900s, and the Houtzdale area was home to the miners whose 1875 conspiracy trials drew national attention. The terrain is mountainous, and the county holds the Quehanna Wild Area, the largest wild area in the state, along with Bilger's Rocks.

The Census Bureau estimated 78,100 residents in July 2025, 3.1 percent fewer people than the 2020 estimates base. The average temperature in DuBois runs from about 24.6 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 68.6 in July.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for a Clearfield County deed?
faqs.a: The posted schedule lists $79.75 for a deed or mortgage, with 50 cents for each name over four and $2 for each page over four. The schedule is marked effective March 27, 2020, so confirm the total with the office at 814-765-2641, extension 5012.

faqs.q: What is the UPI fee in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: It is $10 per parcel, and the stamp must be on a deed before the recorder will accept it. Call 814-765-2641, extension 2042 to ask about pre-approval.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county lists Simplifile (800-460-5657) and CSC (866-652-0111) as vendors for e-recording deeds. Contact one of them to start.

faqs.q: When is a Statement of Value required in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: It is required when the deed does not state full consideration, when the transfer is a gift, when an exemption is claimed, for tax claim and sheriff sales, and when property passes by will. A transfer exempt only because of a family relationship does not need one.

faqs.q: Who pays Pennsylvania realty transfer tax?
faqs.a: The 1 percent state tax is a joint liability of buyer and seller, as the Department of Revenue describes it. Check the sales contract for how the cost is split; the tax is gathered at the recording window.
